title: U.S. to propose emergency AI notification system with China
key_facts: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Axios on 3 Oct 2026 that the US will propose a notification process with China for when something goes wrong with AI.
He said he assumes Beijing will agree.
Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng discussed AI safety and an incident reporting workflow ahead of Xi Jinping's state visit last month.
Bessent said China has had a 'sudden epiphany' about the risks of its open-source models, quoting him: 'I think that they didn't realize how powerful their open source models are.'
Risks he named included AI agents and malicious actors using the technology for cyberattacks.
Bessent argued the US should put more effort into protecting critical systems than into making models more powerful.
quote_evidence: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said during a television appearance that he is proposing a communication workflow between the US and China if something goes wrong with AI, on the assumption that Beijing will agree.
In this connection, Bessent said: “I think that they didn't realize how powerful their open source models are.”
why_it_matters_hint: The two biggest AI powers may set up a hotline-style channel for AI incidents, a first formal safety link between them.
notes: Axios blocked (Cloudflare 403); facts from The News International's write-up of the Axios interview. One outlet, a proposal not yet agreed by China.
